records.claim: Carroll & Doherty 2003 Family Relations meta-analysis of premarital prevention programmes: average effect size ~0.80
Fawcett 2010 Family Relations: 47 studies incl. unpublished; no consistent relationship satisfaction/quality gain; clearer communication gains esp. observational

Hawkins 2022 ACF-funded couple relationship education meta-analysis, 32 controlled evaluations: relationship quality d=0.114, relationship skills d=0.132, mental health d=0.074, coparenting d=0.033; stability/parenting/child well-being not significant

Online relationship education meta-analysis, 12 publications: improved satisfaction, communication, confidence; reduced negative qualities; reduced anxiety/depressive symptoms; improved health satisfaction and quality of life

Hawkins/Blanchard? MRE programmatic moderators meta-analysis, 148 evaluation reports (Behavior Therapy 2012?): 9-20 h programmes more effective than short; communication-focused programmes higher communication effects
2024 trial: booklet- vs video-based premarital education, 110 engaged couples; both increased reproductive health literacy incl. access, evaluation, decision-making/application
2026 quasi-experimental: reproductive and sexual health education in premarital counselling classes; knowledge and attitudes improved at 3 months; no clinical outcomes
Couple-based preconception care SR 2026 (Reproductive Health): 14 studies, 10 countries
Proulx 2007 J Marriage Fam meta-analysis: 93 studies; marital quality and personal well-being r=.37 cross-sectional, r=.25 longitudinal

Robles 2014 Psychol Bull meta-analysis: 126 articles, >72,000 participants; marital quality associated with physical health r~.07-.21, lower mortality risk, lower cardiovascular reactivity during conflict
